newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's Droga says 1996 net up 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's Droga says 1996 net up 30 pct.

text.p: Slovenian food maker Droga Portoroz said on Thursday its unrevised 1996 net profit rose 30 percent to 800 million tolars ($5.13 million) as sales rose and operating expenses fell.
"We expect the 1996 dividend will be some 30 percent higher than the 784 tolars per share paid for 1995," chief executive Matjaz Cacovic told a news conference.
He said sales were up 23 percent at 11.4 billion tolars, while exports alone grew 33 percent to two billion tolars.
Droga expects sales to rise 14 percent this year, while pre-tax profit should rise 20 percent from one billion tolars this year.

Exports were expected to rise by a steep 50 percent as sales to other successor republics of the former Yugoslavia boomed, Droga's main market before the break-up of federation in 1991. The company exports as much as 75 percent of its production in those countries, it said.
"We expect to increase our investments to 10 percent of sales in 1997 in order to modernise production, build new factories and establish new products," Cacovic said.
In 1996 Droga spent 800 million tolars or seven percent of its sales on investments.
The company recently acquired an international quality certificate ISO 9001 for most of its products.

Droga's shares were listed on the main market of the Ljubljana bourse in June 1996. Some 24 percent of its shares are held by foreigners, led by Britain's E.D.&F Man Coffee, which alone owns 20 percent of Droga's equity.
On Thursday Droga's shares firmed 0.29 percent to 24,000 tolars. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
